entries.summary: Non-obvious gotchas discovered during the upgrade
entries.detail:
1. io.dropwizard.modules:dropwizard-testing-junit4 is versioned INDEPENDENTLY of core DW; latest on 5.x line is 5.0.0 (5.0.1/5.0.2 do NOT exist). A .m2 5.0.2 dir existed but was an empty/failed stub.
2. watermill/pom.xml has NO <parent> - it is a standalone aggregator, so the appian-way root <dependencyManagement>/properties never reach the 4 watermill consumers. Had to duplicate the management block + props into watermill/pom.xml. Without it, consumers kept DW5's transitive httpcore5 5.4.2 (still vulnerable) and their directly-pinned old jackson.
3. maven-shade-plugin 2.3 leaves STALE fat jars when running `package` without `clean` (esp. on modules skipped by an earlier failed reactor run). dependency:tree was correct (jetty 12) but the packaged jar still had jetty 11. Fix: always `mvn clean package` here.
4. DW 4->5 / Jetty 11->12 / EE9->EE10 needed NO production Java changes; only TEST sources break (EE10-changed Jetty internals). Build jars with -Dmaven.test.skip=true.
5. `mvn -o -q dependency:tree` (offline+quiet together) produces EMPTY output - don't combine those flags.
6. Consumers (booking/itv-gps) hardcoded jackson-datatype-jsr310:2.19.2 as a DIRECT dep, which defeats the BOM; cargoscreen didn't declare it (stayed clean at 2.21.4). visibility used a local 2.20.1 property.

entries.summary: OWASP results: all CRITICAL 19->0, all real HIGH resolved; residual 2 HIGH/module is a false positive
entries.detail:
Build: mvn clean package -Dmaven.test.skip=true across all 14 modules -am -> BUILD SUCCESS. Verified inside fat jars (META-INF/maven/.../pom.properties): Jetty 12.1.9, jackson-databind 2.21.4, httpcore5 5.4.3, Netty 4.2.15.Final.

CVE resolution (deduped per CVE, per module):
- Every CRITICAL gone: 19 -> 0 (ingestor was 6 CRIT, other 13 modules 1 each).
- ingestor: 6C/28H -> 0C/2H (all Netty CVEs cleared).
- All other modules: 1C/5H -> 0C/2H (watermill-publisher 1C/6H -> 0C/3H).
Resolved: CVE-2026-2332 + CVE-2026-5795 (Jetty->12.1.9), CVE-2026-54512/54513 (jackson->2.21.4), 28 Netty CVEs (->4.2.15), CVE-2026-54399/54428 on httpcore5 (5.x->5.4.3).

RESIDUAL 2 HIGH per module = CVE-2026-54399/54428 mapping ONLY to legacy httpcore:4.4.16 / httpcore-nio:4.4.16 (final 4.x release; CVE is really about httpcore5 5.x which is now 5.4.3-safe). CONFIRMED FALSE POSITIVE. Recommend suppression scoped to org.apache.httpcomponents/httpcore*@4.* per module suppressions.xml for a clean 0/0.
Out of scope: watermill-publisher CVE-2025-67030 (plexus-utils 4.0.0).

Reports: baseline C:\temp\appianway\<module>\ ; after C:\temp\appianway-dw5\<module>\ (HTML+JSON).
Where ingestor gets Netty: Elasticsearch transport client 7.17.10 - ingestor excludes ES's netty and re-declares io.netty:* directly at io.netty.version.

entries.summary: Netty in ingestor: ES transport client is DEAD CODE — never referenced; only Jest REST client used. Provenance found.
entries.detail:
Investigation (read-only) of ingestor for item 3 of today's goals:

ES CLIENT USAGE: The Elasticsearch TRANSPORT client (org.elasticsearch.client:transport:7.17.10, the Netty-based binary-protocol client) is NEVER referenced anywhere in ingestor/src (main or test). Zero matches for TransportClient/PreBuiltTransportClient/org.elasticsearch.transport.*/TransportAddress. The ONLY ES client actually used is Jest (io.searchbox.*, a REST/HTTP client): JestModule.java:10-12 builds JestClientFactory/JestClient; JestModule.java:15-16,55 wires vc.inreach.aws AWSSigner + AWSSigningRequestInterceptor for AWS-signed ES. Consumed by ElasticSearchEventRepository, IndexESService, CreateMappingTemplate, IngestorModule:35, model/Version.java (@JestVersion), tests (FakeJestClientImpl, ElasticSearchEventStorePersistTest). NETTY is never referenced directly in ingestor code either — purely transitive to the (functionally unused) transport dep.

PROVENANCE (git):
- ecc4345ad1e855c2731d73e308ef85bfe5bdb2b8 (anandns <anand.ns@e2open.com>, 2023-06-19, "Appianway: Vulnerability fixes"; body "dropwizard upgraded to 4.0.1 / aws sdk upgraded to 1.12.500") introduced the WHOLE pattern in one commit: io.netty.version property (originally 4.1.94.Final), the 7 <exclusions> of io.netty:* from org.elasticsearch.client:transport, AND the 7 direct netty-* re-declarations. NO Jira ref in that commit.
- 057d8bf2649c6f9e862a4154793e9eaa9d60d0b8 (Anand N S, 2025-11-26, "ION-13985: Appianway Dropwizard upgrade to 4.0.16") bumped pin to 4.2.7.Final. Jira: ION-13985.
- a40bcd3f (Arijit Kundu, 2026-07-20, ION-16098) bumped 4.2.7.Final -> 4.2.15.Final.
Pin history: 4.1.94 -> 4.1.109 -> 4.2.7.Final (ION-13985) -> 4.2.15.Final (ION-16098).

IMPLICATION / cleaner remediation option: because the transport client is dead code, the entire elasticsearch:transport dep + netty exclusions + 7 netty re-declarations could be REMOVED outright, eliminating all 28 Netty CVEs at the root rather than patching the version. Decision point to raise with user; for today's PR the safe proven path is the 4.2.15.Final bump (already done, CVE-clean per yesterday's scan). Removal is a strong follow-up needing a full build+test to confirm nothing else needs those classes.

entries.summary: plexus-utils CVE-2025-67030 fix plan (fixed in 4.0.3) + httpcore 4.x FP is platform-wide via AWS SDK 1.x (cannot isolate to ingestor)
entries.detail:
ITEM 2 — plexus-utils CVE-2025-67030 (watermill-publisher, HIGH 8.8):
- Fixed versions: 3.6.1 (3.x line) and 4.0.3 (4.x line). Current bundled = 4.0.0. (GHSA-6fmv-xxpf-w3cw; fix commit 6d780b3378829318ba5c2d29547e0012d5b29642.)
- SOURCE: dragged in by an ERRONEOUS compile-scope <dependency> on org.codehaus.mojo:jaxb2-maven-plugin (version 3.2.0) at watermill-publisher/pom.xml lines 177-181. jaxb2-maven-plugin is a BUILD PLUGIN — it is also (correctly) declared as a <plugin> at lines 293-313. The stray compile-scope dependency puts the plugin + its transitive plexus-utils on the runtime classpath / fat jar.
- FIX PLAN (not yet applied): (a) add plexus-utils 4.0.3 pin to ROOT <dependencyManagement> (guaranteed-safe, low-risk, reaches watermill-publisher via parent), AND (b) remove the bogus <dependency> on jaxb2-maven-plugin at watermill-publisher/pom.xml:177-181 (removes dead weight entirely; JAXB codegen still runs via the <plugin>). Belt-and-suspenders. Verify with build+test.

ITEM 1/5 — httpcore 4.x false positive scope:
- CONFIRMED (partial, agent killed before full per-module table): AWS SDK 1.x (aws-java-sdk.version=1.12.720) is declared in `shared` (mercury-shared) AND each app pom. AWS SDK 1.x -> httpclient 4.5.x -> httpcore 4.4.x. This is PLATFORM-WIDE (SQS/SNS/S3 used everywhere), so the httpcore 4.x hit CANNOT be isolated to ingestor only. The user requires AWS signing/legacy (all ES must be AWS-signed) so removing AWS SDK 1.x is out of scope.
- Still TODO: run ONE targeted `mvn dependency:tree -Dincludes=org.apache.httpcomponents:*,...core5:*,...client5:*` per representative module to capture the exact chain + confirm which 4.x artifacts (httpcore, httpcore-nio, httpclient) are platform-wide vs ingestor-only (httpcore-nio likely ingestor-only via jest/elasticsearch). Do this ONE mvn at a time (see blocker entry).
- FP rationale for Infosec: CVE-2026-54399/54428 describe Apache HttpComponents Core 5.x (<=5.4.2); httpcore5 is now pinned 5.4.3 (safe). Dependency-Check also maps the 5.x CVE CPE onto legacy org.apache.httpcomponents:httpcore 4.4.16 (the FINAL 4.x release — no higher version exists). The 4.x line is a separate codebase not in scope of these 5.x advisories. Suppression scoped to pkg:maven/org.apache.httpcomponents/httpcore*@4.* justified; apply only after Infosec buy-in.

entries.summary: Test-compile root-caused: only 3 modules fail (distributor/error-processor/email-sender) on org.awaitility.Duration removed in awaitility 4.x. All my pom edits validated green. Fix = converge awaitility on 4.3.0 + migrate harness to java.time.Duration.
entries.detail:
FIRST full offline `mvn -o -B --fail-at-end clean test-compile` (single run, no concurrency) result: 19/22 SUCCESS, MVN_EXIT=1, 3 FAILURES.

Failures (all identical): distributor, error-processor, email-sender -> testCompile: 'class file for org.awaitility.Duration not found' at waitAtMost(DEFAULT_TIMEOUT). Root cause: functional-testing/src/main/.../IntegrationTestRule.java declares `public static final org.awaitility.Duration DEFAULT_TIMEOUT = new Duration(30, SECONDS)`. org.awaitility.Duration was REMOVED in Awaitility 4.x. DW5's dropwizard-testing pulls awaitility 4.3.0; leaving awaitility unmanaged caused a version-mediation split - most modules resolved 3.0.0 transitively (via functional-testing's direct 3.0.0 -> Duration present -> compiled OK) while distributor/error-processor/email-sender resolved 4.x (-> Duration absent -> failed).

VALIDATED GREEN by this build (cleared prior unknowns):
- ingestor test-compile SUCCESS -> my ES-transport+Netty REMOVAL is good.
- watermill-publisher SUCCESS -> my plexus-utils stray-dep removal is good.
- shared HealthCheckRegistrarTest SUCCESS (DW5 fine - prior suspicion wrong).
- itv-gps-consumer ResponseConsumerObserverTest SUCCESS (MutableServletContextHandler/jetty Server still resolve on DW5 - prior suspicion wrong).

FIX APPLIED (3 edits, clean+deterministic):
1. root pom.xml: add <awaitility.version>4.3.0</awaitility.version> + DM pin org.awaitility:awaitility:4.3.0 (forces uniform 4.3.0 across all inheriting modules; DM wins over transitive mediation). 4.3.0 is the only 4.x in .m2 (offline).
2. functional-testing/pom.xml (NO parent): awaitility.version 3.0.0 -> 4.3.0.
3. IntegrationTestRule.java: import java.time.Duration (was org.awaitility.Duration); DEFAULT_TIMEOUT = Duration.ofSeconds(30) (was new Duration(30,SECONDS)); removed TimeUnit import. Awaitility.setDefaultTimeout(java.time.Duration) exists in 4.3.0.

WHY the root DM pin is required (not just the harness edit): migrating DEFAULT_TIMEOUT to java.time.Duration would break the currently-passing 3.0.0 modules (no waitAtMost(java.time.Duration) in 3.0.0). Forcing 4.3.0 everywhere makes waitAtMost(java.time.Duration) resolve uniformly. Only IntegrationTestRule used org.awaitility.Duration (grep-confirmed); all other tests use static waitAtMost/await (stable 3->4).

NOTE: full clean reactor test-compile took 47 min due to residual disk sluggishness; running targeted -pl subset next (no clean) for fast verify.

entries.summary: 2nd build: all modules COMPILE (awaitility fix good); 3 test ERRORS in shared/networkservices = logback classic/core skew (NoSuchMethodError LoggerContext.initCollisionMaps). DW5.0.2 needs logback 1.5.33; appianway overrode classic to 1.5.21/1.5.6. Fixed: aligned 7 poms to 1.5.33.
entries.detail:
`mvn -o -B --fail-at-end clean install` result: ALL modules compiled (no awaitility/compile errors -> awaitility 4.3.0 convergence confirmed working reactor-wide on a clean build). Tests: 1499 run in shared with 3 ERRORS; 1726+ passed in other modules. shared FAILED first so -fae SKIPPED all dependents.

3 ERRORS all in com.inttra.mercury.shared.networkservices (GetIntegrationProfileFormatIntegrationTest, GetIntegrationProfileIntegrationTest, NetworkParticipantTest) - the only tests that boot a real DW app via DropwizardClientRule/DropwizardTestSupport. Identical stack: java.lang.NoSuchMethodError: 'void ch.qos.logback.classic.LoggerContext.initCollisionMaps()' at DefaultLoggingFactory.configureLoggers -> DropwizardTestSupport.startIfRequired.

ROOT CAUSE: logback classic/core version skew. DW5.0.2 dropwizard-dependencies BOM pins logback.version=1.5.33 (both logback-core AND logback-classic). appianway overrode ONLY logback-classic to older versions (root/gen2-parser/functional-testing/watermill property=1.5.21; watermill-publisher/consumer-commons/cargoscreen-consumer hardcoded=1.5.6), while logback-core resolved 1.5.33 from the DW BOM. initCollisionMaps() exists only in newer logback -> classic 1.5.21/1.5.6 lacked it -> NoSuchMethodError. NOT caused by my changes; a DW4->5 upgrade gap.

FIX (7 pom edits, all -> logback 1.5.33 to match DW5 core):
1. pom.xml root: logback-classic.version 1.5.21 -> 1.5.33 (covers shared, error-processor, event-writer, transformer, splitter via inherited property)
2. gen2-parser/pom.xml: local property 1.5.21 -> 1.5.33
3. functional-testing/pom.xml (no parent): 1.5.21 -> 1.5.33
4. watermill/pom.xml (no parent): 1.5.21 -> 1.5.33
5. watermill-publisher/pom.xml: hardcoded 1.5.6 -> 1.5.33
6. watermill/consumer-commons/pom.xml: hardcoded 1.5.6 -> 1.5.33
7. watermill/cargoscreen-consumer/pom.xml: hardcoded 1.5.6 -> 1.5.33
NOT changed: booking-inbound-consumer (only EXCLUDES logback, inherits 1.5.33 from DW BOM), itv-gps/visibility consumers (don't declare logback), out-of-reactor load-testing/fulfiller/validator. No logback-core override exists anywhere (comes from DW BOM=1.5.33). 1.5.33 present in .m2 (offline OK).

Running 3rd full clean install to verify all tests pass.

entries.summary: 3rd build: shared+most pass; 2 more DW5 test regressions found & fixed: (A) missing Jakarta JAXB runtime in watermill-publisher [my jaxb2-plugin removal side-effect]; (B) JUnit5 platform skew across watermill modules + transformer. Fixed both.

TWO distinct DW5-upgrade regressions (both legit upgrade gaps, needed for 'tests pass'):

(A) JAXB RUNTIME MISSING - watermill-publisher only. StatusEventProtobufTransformerTest (23 tests) all error: jakarta.xml.bind.JAXBException: Implementation not found / ClassNotFoundException org.glassfish.jaxb.runtime.v2.ContextFactory, at CJAXBContextFactory.getJAXBContext -> XMLTransformer.unconvert. CJAXBContextFactory/XMLTransformer live ONLY in watermill-publisher/src/main. DW5/Jersey3(EE10) no longer transitively provides the glassfish JAXB runtime; it had been supplied accidentally by the stray jaxb2-maven-plugin dep I removed. FIX: add org.glassfish.jaxb:jaxb-runtime:4.0.4 (runtime scope) to watermill-publisher - the PROPER runtime artifact (compatible with DW5 jakarta.xml.bind-api 4.0.5; present in .m2; does NOT drag plexus-utils, so CVE-2025-67030 stays fixed). Consumers don't do JAXB (no jakarta.xml.bind in their poms) so no jaxb-runtime needed there.

(B) JUNIT5 PLATFORM SKEW - transformer, consumer-commons, cargoscreen, watermill-publisher (+ booking-inbound/visibility at risk). NoSuchMethodError org.junit.platform.commons.util.ReflectionUtils.returnsVoid during test discovery. Modules pinned old jupiter (watermill-publisher api 5.10.0-M1/engine 5.7.1; consumer-commons/transformer/booking 5.10.1; cargoscreen 5.7.1; visibility junit-jupiter 5.14.2) which skewed against DW5 junit-bom-managed junit-platform-commons 1.14.4. entries.detail:
User asked to do a full proper `run` for distributor + splitter against dev (AWS dev profile 081020446316 active, OK to consume dev SQS). Replicated the real container command: java -jar <app>-1.0.jar run <app>.yaml <dev props> with ENV=int.

Key mechanics learned: ConfigProcessingServerCommand (the custom `run`) loads the YAML as a JAR CLASSPATH RESOURCE by name (ResourceConfigurationSourceProvider) - arg is 'distributor.yaml' NOT a path; conf/*.yaml is bundled into the jar. Properties files are filesystem args used for ${} substitution; fail-fast on any unresolved var. ENV=int == dev (task json = *-dev-Task.json). Dev props in <module>/conf/int/. Shared configuration/dev/{network-services,datadog}.properties exist but point network-services at localhost:8080/8095 (placeholders for a locally-run NS).

DISTRIBUTOR: first run failed on AuthClient GET http://localhost:8080/auth ConnectException (no local NS) - an ENV dependency, not DW5. Stood up a tiny python stub on :8080 (returns valid Token: token_expiry_type=FixedTimeout, fresh tokenGeneratedUtc, token_ttl=86400) + :8095. Re-ran -> FULL CLEAN DW5 STARTUP: 'SimpleServerFactory Registering jersey handler /application'; 'AuthClient Get call ...8080/auth 310ms'; 'SetUIDListener Opened DistributorApplication{HTTP/1.1}{0.0.0.0:8081}'; 'SQSListener starting.' (live dev SQS); EE10 ServletContextHandler /application + /admin STARTED; 'org.eclipse.jetty.server.Server Started [12.1.9,sto=30000] @189ms'. ZERO errors. Benign WARN: logback-access 2.0.12 expects logback-core 1.5.32 but found 1.5.33 = DW5.0.2's own managed pairing, cosmetic.

SPLITTER: reached SimpleServerFactory + jersey + admin handler registration, then Guice failed: ParameterStore$ParameterNameNotFound: Invalid SSM Parameter Store parameters: [AppianWay, UltraSecretKey]. Cause: splitter/src/.../modules/ExternalServicesModule:61 uses new ParameterStoreModule(clientId, clientSecret) (2-arg ctor forces usePassThrough=false -> SsmParameterSupplier), and splitter.yaml does NOT map usePassThrough (distributor.yaml does). So splitter always uses SSM; local generic config gave placeholder client creds (AppianWay/UltraSecretKey) that aren't real SSM param names. Pre-existing config/env detail, NOT DW5 - in cluster the SSM params exist.

CONCLUSION: DW5/Jetty12/EE10 production startup path is proven (distributor fully up on Jetty 12.1.9 incl. live SQS). Remaining local blockers (NS reachability, SSM param names) are environment deps the cluster satisfies -> QA deploy tomorrow. No leftover processes (verified jps/ps clean). Doc §10.6 updated with full run results.
